title: Pricing SKU bucket assumptions + finance check-in (workpad)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working note ahead of the 2025-02-04 finance check-in. Goal is to: 1) capture the data sources used to populate SKU bucket inputs in the pricing spreadsheet, 2) call out explicit calibration steps where we deviated from raw telemetry, 3) list residual unknowns and risk factors for finance to sign off, and 4) propose a short checklist + decision points for final numbers.

High level summary (what I mean by SKU buckets):
- Hosted API - small / medium / large model flavors (examples: small = 7B-ish, medium = 13–30B, large = 70B+)
- Hosted API - embedding / rerank SKU (token vs tokenless billing differences)
- Dedicated reserved capacity - committed GPU pools (per-month SKU)
- Private (VPC / on-prem) - license + install + support bundle

Key inputs we currently populate in spreadsheet (source + current nominal value / delta range):
1) Average tokens per request (prod logs): 45 tokens (range 25–80) — source: prod-telemetry.tokens-per-request daily aggregate, sample period Nov 1–Dec 31 2024. Calibrated down 10% to account for SDK trimming and prefilled system prompts.
2) Avg sequence length (seq_len distribution): 480 tokens/session for long-chat flows, 70 for short-gen. We split buckets; Hosted-large uses 480 nominal, hosted-small uses 90.
3) QPS and concurrency profiles: P95 concurrency = 120k bursts/day; baseline sustained QPS used in model = 6k (from request patterns, 90-day rolling).
4) Effective batching factor (experiment + runtime telemetry): nominal batch factor = 6 for 2048 context on our runtime; sensitivity 4–10. Source: bench/serve/batching-experiments-2024 and runtime-metrics.batch-size-dist. Note: dedicated reserved pools see factor +2 due to predictable traffic.
5) GPU token throughput & GPU-hours per 1M tokens: computed from benchmarks (see linked spreadsheet). Nominal: 0.18 GPU-hours / 1M tokens for medium quantized profile; range 0.12–0.30 depending on sequence length and quantization.
6) Cloud GPU cost / hour: spot vs on-demand blended price = $2.80/hr nominal (source: infra procurement discounts + GCP/EC2 price sheet Q4 2024). Blended because we assumed 65% spot usage on hosted pools.
7) Overhead multiplier (network, infra infra services, SRE, storage): 1.28x on raw GPU cost — derived from cost-of-running pipeline (logs, orch, storage) and estimated team SRE/infra headcount chargebacks.
8) Customer support & account ops allocation: $0.06 / 1k tokens equivalent for hosted (absorb into gross margin layer).
9) Amortized model licensing / transfer cost (for some closed-source models we pay per-inference fees): included as $0.003 / 1K tokens where applicable (rare).

Data sources and provenance (where each number came from):
- Prod telemetry (primary): aggregated from telemetry-prod.token-aggregates and runtime request logs. Stored as daily CSV in infra-metrics bucket.
- Benchmarks: bench/serve/series/2024-12 (contains scripts and raw runs for 1–8k batch sizes). These runs were on rtx-8000-equivalent and A100 variants; we used A100-equivalent normalized throughput when calculating GPU-hours.
- Infra ledger (finance): COGS lines for GPU invoices (Q3–Q4 2024), network charges, and reserved instance discounts. Used to derive blended GPU-hour cost.
- Sales & contracts: dedicated customer price lists used for margin sanity checks and amortization expectations.
- Engineering estimates: padding applied for headroom, from SRE/serving-runtime team notes. See linked PRs: github.com/redwood/serve#PR-2147 (batching changes) and eng/serving-runtime/notes/batching-playback.md.

Calibration decisions (explicit deviations from raw telemetry and why):
- Tokens per request: reduced by 10% from raw to reflect SDK-side prompt trimming and upstream router truncation we observed in beta logs. Rationale: production customers will enable prefilled prompts and our client libs apply trimming that telemetry doesn't cleanly reflect.
- Effective batching: reduced nominal batching by 1.5x for hosted small bucket vs bench-run numbers because real traffic is bursty and multi-tenant. We documented the distribution of empty slots and impact on throughput in bench notes.
- Spot utilization: we assume 65% spot blended pricing for hosted. Finance queried this; we used historical spot eviction rates and capacity signals. If spot drops to 40% the blended GPU cost moves ~+27%.
- Overhead multiplier: set to 1.28x rather than 1.15x after including trial SRE oncall overtime and expanded observability retention for the product cohort. This was an upward calibration mainly from finance's review of Q4 infra spend.

Sensitivity notes (quick guide for reviewers):
- GPU cost/hr +/-20% -> unit cost impact +/− 20–22% (linear).
- Batching factor variations are non-linear: when batch factor goes from 6 -> 4, GPU-hours / token increases ~35% for long contexts.
- Prefix-KV cache coverage (% of tokens served from cache) unknown: if cache coverage >20% for expected workloads, effective GPU-hours / token reduces materially (~10–30%). We currently model 5% cache coverage for hosted.

Open questions / risks to call out for finance sign-off:
- Double counting: some host-level caching benefits and application-layer deduplication were both partially applied in the spreadsheet. Need a single canonical path (either apply cache effect at request-level or at GPU throughput level).
- Customer churn on dedicated SKUs: committed pool utilization assumptions assume 85% utilization of commits on average; historical retention suggests 78% for Q4 cohorts. This difference matters for revenue recognition and COGS matching.
- Tail-latency SLO penalty model doesn't exist in the spreadsheet. We should bake in an average SLA credit cost for 0.5% of revenue for hosted-large SKU as an insurance line.
- Spot availability sensitivity: worst-case blended GPU cost under low spot availability and high demand months (seasonality) needs explicit scenario in the model.

Proposed immediate next steps (for the 02/04 meeting):
- Finance to confirm blended GPU cost calc and acceptance of 65% spot assumption OR provide target blended price to use. (Owner: Priya)
- Eng (bench team) to reproduce two benchmark runs with the exact quantization/config used in spreadsheet and attach raw logs to sheet. (Owner: Ben)
- Product to remove duplicated cache adjustments and commit to where cache is applied in the model (request layer vs GPU layer). (Owner: Maya)
- Customer success to provide 3 representative dedicated customer utilization histories for last 12 months (anonymized) to validate 85% assumption. (Owner: Samantha)

Draft sign-off checklist for finance (minimal):
- [ ] Confirm blended GPU $/hr and share invoice sample lines used to compute it (documented).
- [ ] Approve overhead multiplier or propose a replacement value with rationale.
- [ ] Accept or revise support & ops allocation line.
- [ ] Confirm that SLA credit line is required and recommend percentage.
- [ ] Sign off on final conservative ranges and label the model as "finance-approved-draft" with an expiry (recommended 90 days).

Appendix: quick snapshot of current nominal per-SKU outputs (from sheet tab 'SKU-nominals' as of 2025-02-02):
- Hosted-small (gen): tokens/request 35, GPU-hrs / 1M tokens = 0.09, blended cost / 1M tokens = $252, gross margin estimate = 62%
- Hosted-medium (gen): tokens/request 120, GPU-hrs / 1M tokens = 0.18, blended cost / 1M tokens = $504, gross margin estimate = 51%
- Hosted-large (gen): tokens/request 480, GPU-hrs / 1M tokens = 0.95, blended cost / 1M tokens = $2660, gross margin estimate = 44%
- Dedicated-reserved (per-month pool): amortized cost per effective vGPU-hr = $1.90 (after commit discount), modeled utilization = 85%

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- I'm intentionally conservative on cache coverage and batching for the first pass. If we get customer data showing higher cache usage we can materially lower hosted units.
- If finance pushes blended GPU/hr significantly lower, we'll flag in pricing docs that margins will expand and consider list price adjustments for ARR targets.
- This doc is a workpad — expect fragments, TODOs, and links to bench logs. Please push edits in the sheet and add comments rather than rewriting this note in full.

-- Maya
